subtopic: Pod Lifecycle, Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes
question_text:
### Production Incident Scenario:
Production Incident #22: A multi-tenant Kubernetes cluster suffered widespread Pod CrashLoopBackOff and node eviction events in Container Orchestration (Kubernetes). Several critical ingress pods were repeatedly terminated with OOMKilled (Exit Code 137) during 'Pod Lifecycle, Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes'.

### Engineering Challenge:
How should the platform team configure Kubernetes resource management and probe semantics to stabilize 'Pod Lifecycle, Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes'?

options.text: Set explicit memory limits matching container cgroup allocations, tune JVM/runtime heap ratios (MaxRAMPercentage), and configure startup probes with sufficient failureThreshold.
Remove all memory and CPU resource limits so containers can consume unbounded host physical memory.
Configure liveness probes to execute an intensive 5-second database write query every 500ms.
Disable container restart policies by setting restartPolicy: Never across all deployments.

answer_explanation: OOMKilled exit code 137 occurs when a container breaches its cgroup memory limit. Aligning runtime heap allocation (e.g., -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75) with Kubernetes limits, accompanied by startup probes to decouple initial warm-up from liveness kills, ensures container resilience.
reference_solution: Recommended Remediation: Option A. Rationale: OOMKilled exit code 137 occurs when a container breaches its cgroup memory limit. Aligning runtime heap allocation (e.g., -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75) with Kubernetes limits, accompanied by startup probes to decouple initial warm-up from liveness kills, ensures container resilience.
